issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before empty-domain check, masking the intended runtime error
issues.detail: In panLog and zoomLog, `Math.sign(domain[0])` is evaluated before `pan`/`zoom` runs the `isNonEmpty` check. For an empty domain, `domain[0]` is `undefined`, so `Math.sign` returns NaN and the helper builds nonsense `log`/`exp` functions before the throw fires inside `pan`. Works today but is fragile — move the empty check up front or assert before computing `sign`.

issues.description: coerceNumber silently substitutes 0 for null/NaN inputs, changing observable behavior
issues.detail: Previously `panLinear`/`zoomLinear` used `toNumber` directly as `lift`, so a domain like `[null, 10]` produced NaN arithmetic. The new `coerceNumber: x => toNumber(x) ?? 0` converts null/undefined into 0 instead, which silently shifts the returned domain rather than propagating NaN. The PR claims `runtime behavior should be the same`; this contradicts that.

issues.description: Domain return type [number, number] is a lie when lift/ground produce NaN or Infinity
issues.detail: `Domain = [number, number]` is returned unconditionally, but `log(sign)` on a domain whose sign flips, or `pow` with fractional exponents on negatives, can yield NaN/Infinity. The type advertises a clean numeric pair while the implementation may emit NaN. Either narrow the type, or document that NaN is a legal `number` here.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw is only tested for panLinear and zoomLinear
issues.detail: The new tests cover only `panLinear([], …)` and `zoomLinear([], null, …)`. The other six exported entry points (`panLog`, `panPow`, `panSymlog`, `zoomLog`, `zoomPow`, `zoomSymlog`) share the same precondition but are not exercised, and as noted above the Log variants take a different code path before reaching the check.

issues.description: peek overload may surprise callers passing a mutable non-empty tuple
issues.detail: The new overload `peek<T>(array: readonly [T, ...T[]]): T` is fine, but the parameter type uses `readonly`, so callers with a plain `T[]` that the compiler cannot prove non-empty fall through to `T | undefined`. That is the intent, but pair this with an explicit JSDoc note so downstream TS users know they need a tuple/const-assertion to get the non-undefined return.

issues.description: Anchor type allows null/undefined but downstream callers may not have expected undefined
issues.detail: `Anchor = number | null | undefined` widens the original implicit contract (callers passed `null` explicitly in tests). The `anchor != null` guard handles both, so runtime is fine, but exporting this through public TS types lets callers omit the argument entirely for `zoomPow`/`zoomSymlog`, which is a new API affordance worth confirming is intentional.

review.summary: The TypeScript port is mostly mechanical and safe, but two behavioral regressions slipped in: `coerceNumber` defaulting null to 0 changes how `panLinear`/`zoomLinear` handle non-numeric inputs, and the Log variants compute `Math.sign(domain[0])` before the new empty-domain guard runs, so an empty input produces NaN helpers before the error fires. Tests only cover the empty-domain throw for the linear variants. The `peek` overload and exported `Domain`/`Anchor` types are reasonable but worth tightening or documenting before this becomes the public typing surface.
